codeReview.summary: The feature adds meaningful new test coverage for helper utilities, rate limiting, and /healthz, but it does not satisfy the requested scope. The core-domain tests do not cover the repository operations called out in the feature description, and the /readyz verification misses the required healthy-path and dependency-check assertions.

issues.description: The promised comprehensive core-domain coverage is still missing. The new tests exercise helpers/constants (for example, domain_test.go and operations_test.go) but do not cover the repository methods that implement the requested auth/projects/builds/deployments/operations behavior: CreateUser/FindUserByEmail (lines 23-24), CreateProject/UpdateProject/DeleteProject (41-43), ClaimBuildJob/ClaimBuildJobByID (57-58), ClaimDeployment/ClaimDeploymentByID (69-70), or CreateOperation (78). A grep across **/*_test.go for those method names returns no matches.

The readiness verification is incomplete versus the feature requirements and VAL-BH-012. This file only checks method-not-allowed, content type, and a nil-state 503 response; it never verifies the healthy 200 path, and it never asserts the actor-system/command-gateway readiness checks that the runtime exposes. Grep shows no actor_system or command_gateway assertions in this test file, even though actors/node.go reports those checks.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The backend-worker skill and the handoff compliance signal are out of sync for API-focused test work. The skill requires manual curl-based verification with interactiveChecks entries, but this feature's handoff records only go test/go vet while still marking followedProcedure=true.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The readiness-response contract is not documented in shared state. Actor readiness originates as actor_system/command_gateway checks, but the HTTP server prefixes actor-node checks under actors.* and uses a generic actors=down shortcut when the node is nil. Without documenting that shape, workers can easily write weaker /readyz assertions.
